title: A new relay generation mid-playback is appended to the existing SourceBuffer without abort() or changeType()
test: tests/browser/media-flow.spec.mjs: 'a playing relay viewer follows the host recorder from MP4 to VP8' and 'a relay viewer that is behind keeps playing across a VP8 recorder restart' (Playwright, Chromium, real server and host; both failed on the unchanged build and pass on the fix, 3 of 3 repeats); tests/watchPlaybackMode.test.js: 'a new relay generation on a playing SourceBuffer resets its parser first', 'a new relay generation in another format switches the SourceBuffer type after the reset', 'a SourceBuffer that cannot take the new relay generation is reported, not reused'. Probe: .arbitra/dev-notes/results/check-19-mse-probe.cjs.txt with check-19-mse-probe-page.js.txt (real MediaRecorder + MSE in Chromium 153 and Firefox 155), output check-19-mse-probe-output.txt
proof: The claim is about src/WatchView.jsx startRelayPlayback (the browser-host MediaRecorder relay: onMediaInit, selectedGeneration, WebM/EBML), not src/lib/fmp4RelayPlayer.js; WatchView.jsx is byte-identical at ac1c688, and the host restart logic (HostView.jsx 1262-1301: frame rate, resolution, bitrate and the MP4-to-VP8 fallback all restart the recorder) and the server relay are unchanged, so it was real on the original code too. onMediaInit (WatchView.jsx 497-513 before the fix) flushes the queue and moves selectedGeneration and mimeType but leaves the SourceBuffer as it was: no abort(), no changeType(). Two failures follow. (1) Chromium's MediaRecorder ends every timeslice one byte into the next WebM element (EBML walk of recorded bytes: all 9 and 12 chunk ends at '+1' into a SimpleBlock, BlockGroup or Cluster), so when old-generation chunks are still queued at the new media-init and flushed, the parser is left inside an element: in the probe the SourceBuffer then took all 13 appends of the new generation and buffered none of them (buffered stuck at [0,2.42], no error event, MediaSource open, no video error); with abort() it buffered to 6.1 s. (2) MP4 to VP8 (lib/socket.js onError emits relay-mp4-failed and expects viewers to 'pick up' the new generation; HostView's MP4 recorder.onerror does the same): the MP4 SourceBuffer swallowed the VP8 generation the same way (buffered stuck at 2.94 s); with abort()+changeType() it reached 7.04 s. The claim's consequence is slightly off: Chromium raises no parse error and does not end the MediaSource; the picture freezes silently and the queue never overflows, so no error is shown either. Firefox's recorder cuts at element boundaries, so Firefox-recorded VP8 survives the flush. E2E on the unchanged build (check-19-e2e-before.txt): MP4 to VP8 'Expected: > 4.528974 Received: 3.148159' (video frozen after the switch), viewer behind across a frame-rate restart 'Expected: > 4.4882919999999995 Received: 1.488292'. Fix (commit 231a8f8 on lane/client): new prepareSourceBufferForGeneration(sourceBuffer, mediaSource, {fromMimeType, toMimeType}) in src/lib/watchPlaybackMode.mjs calls abort() and, when the type changes, changeType(); WatchView's onMediaInit calls it once this attempt has a SourceBuffer and, if it returns false (MediaSource not open, no changeType, or the browser refuses the type), ends the attempt through failRelayGeneration with RELAY_PLAYBACK_UNSUPPORTED_MESSAGE or 'Relay playback could not follow the new stream and must be restarted.'. Both e2e tests pass after it (check-19-e2e-after.txt). The unit tests failed before only because the helper did not exist. Checks: npm run lint and npm run typecheck clean; npm test 1054/1054; npx playwright test --workers=1: 62 passed, 13 skipped, 3 failed, the 3 tests of tests/browser/host-obs-control-channel.spec.mjs, which fail the same way on the unchanged build (also in check-19-e2e-before.txt). src/lib/fmp4RelayPlayer.js (OBS fMP4 relay) does not have this defect: handleMediaInit calls changeType through switchSourceBufferType or rebuilds the MediaSource, and its chunks are whole moof+mdat fragments (lib/fmp4Parser.js), so its parser is always at a box boundary.
